newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asia Metals - S.Korean Q3 aluminium premiums at $95.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals - S.Korean Q3 aluminium premiums at $95.

text.p: South Korean aluminium import premiums for the third quarter are being settled at around $95 a tonne over London Metal Exchange's (LME) cash average prices, following higher Japanese premiums, traders said on Thursday.
This compares with $88 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME cash average prices for second quarter shipment, they said.
"Some local traders said they have settled aluminium import premium for the third quarter at around $95," one trader said.
Traders said the metal's premiums for spot trade were barely changed in a range between $93 to $100 a tonne over LME cash average prices over the past week.

Meanwhile, local copper traders said LG Metals Corp, an affiliate of LG Group and South Korea's largest copper producer, is expected to raise its monthly domestic selling price for June from 2,354,000 won a tonne in May in line with recent gains in LME prices.
They said recent copper import premiums for grade A, spot delivery, rose to $80 to $85 a tonne from $75 to $80 over LME cash prices a week ago due to strong global demand.
But, zinc import premiums for Chinese special high grade fell to $20 to $30 a tonne for spot delivery from the previous $30 to $35 due to an increase in Chinese imports.
Traders said China's zinc exports were increasing to cash-in on current strong LME prices.
They added Korea Zinc is expected to raise its monthly domestic selling price by 70,000 to 80,000 won a tonne in June from 1,283,000 won in May.

But the majority of South Korean aluminium importers have yet to conclude third quarter agreements with foreign suppliers as they are hesitating over a slowdown in the country's economy after a series of corporate crises.

In Japan, aluminium import premiums for the quarter were settling at between $86 to $87 a tonne, up $5 a tonne from the second quarter, reflecting strong global demand for the metal and low LME stocks.
The premium levels for Japanese buyers are traditionally a benchmark indicator for South Korean import deals.
